conclusion.tests_summary: 8 cases were tested; 1 of them reached raw p < 0.05 (london_large_roofs p=0.023). After Bonferroni correction (alpha = 0.05/8 = 0.00625) 0 remain, and after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction 0 remain.
conclusion.resolution_finding: The roof-to-pixel area ratio rose from 0.016 (london_small_roofs) to 0.915 (london_large_roofs_ecostress, p=0.18), yet the signal did not strengthen: no case is significant after correction. Resolution is therefore not the only problem.
untested_explanations: Emissivity: bright bare-metal roofs have a low thermal emissivity, so they shed heat poorly and the satellite retrieval, which assumes a generic emissivity, misreads their temperature; albedo alone does not decide the measured LST.
Albedo error: the Sentinel-2 broadband albedo is an estimate (Liang 2001 narrow-to-broadband conversion at 20 m), so some roofs may sit in the wrong albedo quartile.
Seasonal median: a summer median of cloud-free scenes smooths out the hot-day differences that a cool roof is meant to reduce.
Location: the dark and bright groups are different buildings in different places, so neighbourhood, height and construction differences are mixed into the comparison.
conclusion.verdict: Satellite data is not sufficient for roof-level verification; it is sufficient for targeting.
conclusion.text: 8 cases were tested; 1 of them reached raw p < 0.05 (london_large_roofs p=0.023). After Bonferroni correction (alpha = 0.05/8 = 0.00625) 0 remain, and after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction 0 remain. The roof-to-pixel area ratio rose from 0.016 (london_small_roofs) to 0.915 (london_large_roofs_ecostress, p=0.18), yet the signal did not strengthen: no case is significant after correction. Resolution is therefore not the only problem. Possible causes not tested here: Emissivity: bright bare-metal roofs have a low thermal emissivity, so they shed heat poorly and the satellite retrieval, which assumes a generic emissivity, misreads their temperature; albedo alone does not decide the measured LST. Albedo error: the Sentinel-2 broadband albedo is an estimate (Liang 2001 narrow-to-broadband conversion at 20 m), so some roofs may sit in the wrong albedo quartile. Seasonal median: a summer median of cloud-free scenes smooths out the hot-day differences that a cool roof is meant to reduce. Location: the dark and bright groups are different buildings in different places, so neighbourhood, height and construction differences are mixed into the comparison. Satellite data is not sufficient for roof-level verification; it is sufficient for targeting.

caveat: Observational comparison between different buildings, not a controlled before/after experiment.
